nomad_manual.man_intro_1: The Flotilla is a population of migrants living aboard your ships. The Flotilla's population and stores are separate from your own cargo and crew.
nomad_manual.man_basics_1: The Flotilla has {{Berths}} and {{Space}}. {{Berths}} are where the population live, and limits how many residents can live in the Flotilla. {{Space}} is used for either (1) storing resource commodities, (2) creating {{Allocations}}, which generally produce resources, or (3) creating {{Works}}, which buff your Flotilla in various ways (e.g. making {{Allocations}} more efficient). You will need to carefully balance {{Space}} and {{Berths}} (e.g. you should not build all {{Works}} because they will both require staffing and take up space, often a scaling percentage of your total space).
nomad_manual.man_basics_2: You add ships to the Flotilla by adding the Nomad hullmod, which will convert a portion of the quarters to {{Berths}} and cargo to {{Space}}. You can adjust the portion which defaults to {dedication_default} (also the minimum) by pressing the button on the Nomad hullmod.
nomad_manual.man_balance_1: In {{Survival}} difficulty (the default, that you can change in LunaLib settings), the Flotilla should be able to cover its needs to start, and by late game should also be able to cover the supply of ships in the Flotilla with some excess.
nomad_manual.man_balance_2: In {{Story}} difficulty, the Flotilla should start being able to cover its needs plus around half of the supply of ships, and by late game should be able to produce a large multiple of the supply needed for its ships.
nomad_manual.man_balance_3: This balance was calculated using vanilla, without mods, assuming spending 1/3 of your time mining a planet with 1.0x resource deposits.
nomad_manual.man_resources_1:
You can directly transfer resources into the Flotilla. You can {{not}} directly transfer resources out, they have to be transferred automatically. There are three important buttons next to each commodity:
    {{OUT}}: Automatically transfer the excess production of the Flotilla to your inventory. Otherwise, the allocation will not produce (or consume inputs) if the storage is full
    {{IN}}: Automatically transfer the commodity from your inventory to the Flotilla if the Flotilla's storage for that commodity is less than {autotransfer_in}.
    {{SELL}}: Allow the {{Credits}} allocation to automatically sell the commodity if it is above {credits_min_fill} full. Note that {credits_min_fill} < {autotransfer_in} so this can automatically sell things from your inventory, and that the credits allocation is the most direct way to earn an income.
nomad_manual.man_resources_2: Each resource has its own storage maximum, which you can configure (in particular for the automatic buttons above), but {{shares}} the remaining space leftover from {{Allocations}} and {{Works}}.
nomad_manual.man_resources_3: Beside each resource, you can see its predicted net change over time. You can press the balance button to try to automatically add allocations to make that net change 0, but note that the balance button will only add allocations necessary to make the net change 0 (and so will never do things like add credit allocations or fuel production allocations).
nomad_manual.man_the_flagship_1: The flagship is the center of the Nomad Fleet. If the flagship is lost or put in storage, the Flotilla stops, it produces nothing, and its residents leave over time until there is another flagship.
nomad_manual.man_residents_1: Residents staff both allocations and Works. The population grows slowly while every need is met, and up to the berth cap. Migrants also join when you undock at an inhabited colony with berths available, at most once every six months from each colony. You can move crew to and from the Flotilla manually on the Overview tab. Note being understaffed decreases global efficiency, which is strongly not recommended, and allocations that are inactive will still require staff.
nomad_manual.man_residents_2: Every resident consumes Food, Supplies, Domestic Goods, and Luxury Goods each month, whether or not they are working. Each unit of allocated space consumes Heavy Machinery every month (it is not per-resident but instead per unit of allocated space).
nomad_manual.man_detaching_1: You can detach the Flotilla to allow it to travel as its own fleet. Detached, it keeps mining and defends itself if attacked, but it consumes only on its own stores and cannot exchange cargo or crew with your fleet. Its ships consume their monthly supplies from the Flotilla's stores while detached, at the same rate they cost your fleet. Bring your fleet to the detached Flotilla to rejoin.
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_1: Global efficiency is a single multiplier on how much the Flotilla produces. Below 75%, the inputs of allocations scale with the outputs. Above 75%, inputs are fixed but outputs continue increasing. 75% represents the floor of minimum required material to make the output, but as you become more efficient you need fewer inputs for the same output.
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_2:
For example, at these global efficiencies an allocation makes this much output for this much input:
    {{130%}}: {{1.3}} out for {{1}} in
    {{125%}}: {{1.25}} out for {{1}} in
    {{100%}}: {{1}} out for {{1}} in
    {{75%}}: {{0.75}} out for {{1}} in
    {{50%}}: {{0.5}} out for {{0.67}} in
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_3: The primary source of efficiency is staffing percentage: your working residents divided by the staff your allocations and Works need. If your staffing percentage is 50%, your global efficiency is halved.
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_4: Another major factor for global efficiency is shortages. A shortage begins when you run out of a required store. Separate shortages will multiply together. Most shortages also cause population decreases (e.g. famines).
nomad_manual.man_yield_1: {{Yield}} is how much an allocation produces for each unit of Space. Every allocation starts at a base yield, which Works and colony items can raise. Yield scales output and input together, so at double yield an allocation makes twice as much and consumes twice the input. Global efficiency is separate from yield.
nomad_manual.man_production_and_mining_1: Each allocation to Credits sells up to {credits_units} stored unit a month, at {credits_price} of base value. The most expensive good marked SELL on the stores list that is over {credits_min_fill} of its effective cap is sold. Selling earns less than trading the goods yourself; it is there to burn off surplus, especially in longer trips. Allocations with inputs produce nothing until every input it needs is in stock.
nomad_manual.man_production_and_mining_2: Most raw inputs come from a mining allocation. Wait within range of a fully surveyed body and the Flotilla mines on its own, faster where the deposit is richer. Each resource the body has is mined at the full rate, so a body with more resource types mines more. Mining does nothing in hyperspace or over an unsurveyed body.
nomad_manual.man_the_autoforge_1: The autoforge builds ships and weapons in the background, one at a time. Each job needs production points equal to the value of what it builds. While the queue is not empty, the allocation turns stored Metals, Transplutonics, and Heavy Machinery into points, and the points apply to the job at the front until it is complete. Queued jobs begin once their previous job finishes More autoforges produce points faster, but the overall cost of the product is unchanged. Queuing a job takes no materials. The consumption begins only once something is in the queue.
